ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the early stage of viral infection, the organism secretes interferon and acts on the cell receptor IFNAR to cope with the infection. Measles is an acute infectious disease caused by measles virus infection. It is known that human leukocyte differentiation antigen 46 (hCD46) is the main receptor for measles virus invasion of cells, and mice do not have this receptor. Researchers constructed hCD46 transgenic mice for related research, and part of the procedure is shown in the figure. Which two restriction enzyme combination shown in the figure should be selected to insert hCD46 into the plasmid?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the early stage of viral infection, the organism secretes interferon and acts on the cell receptor IFNAR to cope with the infection. It is known that human leukocyte differentiation antigen 46 (hCD46) is the main receptor for measles virus invasion of cells, and mice do not have this receptor. Researchers constructed hCD46 transgenic mice for related research, and part of the procedure is shown in the figure. Which two restriction enzyme combination shown in the figure should be selected to insert hCD46 into the plasmid?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The linear fragment on the left in the figure is labeled hCD46. Above this fragment, restriction enzyme sites EcoRⅠ, SacⅠ, BamHⅠ, and NotⅠ can be seen, with EcoRⅠ near one end and NotⅠ near the other end. In the plasmid diagram on the right, near the insertion region between the promoter and the terminator, EcoRⅠ, SacⅠ, and NotⅠ are labeled; other positions of the plasmid are also labeled with sites such as AgeⅠ and HindⅢ. Then reason: To insert hCD46 into the plasmid, it is necessary to select restriction enzyme sites that are near both ends of the target gene and also exist in the plasmid insertion region, so that hCD46 can be completely cut out and directionally inserted between the promoter and the terminator. EcoRⅠ is located at one end of hCD46 and the plasmid insertion region has the corresponding site; NotⅠ is located at the other end of hCD46 and the plasmid insertion region also has the corresponding site. Although SacⅠ is present in both, it is near the interior of the hCD46 fragment and is not suitable for completely cutting out the target gene; BamHⅠ is not in the corresponding insertion site of the plasmid. Therefore EcoRⅠ and NotⅠ should be selected.
